findings.title: Same concurrent-deletion NPE remains in the getSubGroupsStream overloads
findings.body: The PR guards only getSubGroupsCount(). The three paged/searching getSubGroupsStream overloads at lines 256, 262 and 268 still call modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) with no null check. When the group has been deleted in the database but the cache has not yet been invalidated, modelSupplier.get() returns null and these methods throw the same NullPointerException the PR is meant to fix. The issue is only partly fixed unless these are guarded too.

findings.title: getSubGroupsCount silently returns null instead of a count or an error
findings.body: The NPE is replaced by a null Long. Callers that unbox the result (for example comparisons or arithmetic on getSubGroupsCount()) will now fail with a different NPE far from the cause. The rest of this adapter treats the same condition, a group that is missing from the database, as IllegalStateException("Not found in database") (lines 61 and 74). The behaviour is also inconsistent: when `invalidated` is true, isUpdated() throws, but in the window before invalidation this method returns null. Throwing the same IllegalStateException here, or otherwise defining the contract for a missing group, would be consistent.

findings.title: parentModel can be null in populateGroupHierarchyFromSubGroups and is still dereferenced
findings.body: Line 47 fetches the parent with session.groups().getGroupById(...), which returns null if the parent was deleted concurrently. The null is then passed to groupEvaluator.canView(parentModel) (line 51), to toRepresentation(groupEvaluator, parentModel, full) inside computeIfAbsent (line 57) and to populateSubGroupCount(parentModel, parent) (line 60). The last two dereference it, so this is the same concurrent-access NPE class the PR claims to fix, left unhandled in the group listing path this PR touches.

findings.title: Reader thread is never joined, so the test can pass with exceptions still pending
findings.body: The reader thread is started at line 139 and never joined. After deletedAll.set(true) at line 155, the assertion at line 157 runs immediately. A request that is in flight when the flag is set can still fail and add to caughtExceptions after the assertion has already passed, so the test can report success when the bug is present. The thread should be joined before asserting on caughtExceptions.

findings.title: Stop flag is set outside try/finally and the reader is a non-daemon thread
findings.body: If any groups().group(...).remove() call in the loop at lines 152-154 throws, deletedAll.set(true) at line 155 is never reached. The reader thread then loops forever, hitting the server with no delay, and as a non-daemon thread it keeps the test JVM alive, so a single failure can hang the whole test run. The stop signal should be set in a finally block, the thread should be a daemon or be joined, and the reader should be stopped on failure.

findings.title: Regression test depends on an unguaranteed race and may not reproduce the NPE
findings.body: The NPE needs the reader to hit the window where a group is deleted in the database but still present in the cache, and nothing here forces that interleaving or confirms that the brief listing reaches getSubGroupsCount(). Without the fix the test can still pass on most runs, so it is not a reliable guard. A deterministic check, for example a run-on-server test that removes the group in a second session while the adapter is held, would catch the regression reliably.
